scope: CAMS EAC4 column-integrated aerosol composition over Beijing, 3-hourly, 2020-01 through 2025-12. Produced by scripts/ingest/fetch_cams.py.

files.aerosol_cams.csv: One row per 3-hourly step: aerosol optical depth split by species, a derived dust share, and the model's surface PM fields.

sources.title: CAMS global reanalysis (EAC4)
sources.notes: Satellite retrievals assimilated into a global chemistry-transport model. Native resolution 0.75 degrees (about 80 km) at 3-hourly steps. This is model output constrained by observations, not an observation.

extraction.spatial_reduction: Mean over the one-to-two 0.75-degree cells covering the box, so the series represents Beijing as a whole rather than an arbitrary corner. The grid cannot resolve any within-city variation.
extraction.time_convention: EAC4 timestamps are UTC; the published columns are Beijing local standard time (UTC+8) and join to the station data on year/month/day/hour.

unit_conversions.cams_pm2p5_ugm3: EAC4 publishes PM in kg m-3; multiplied by 1e9 to ug m-3. Reading the raw field without converting yields values that round to 0.0.

derived_fields.dust_fraction: dust_aod550 / total_aod550 — the dust share of column optical depth.

validation.single_event_check: For the 2021-03-15 Beijing sandstorm, dust AOD rose from about 0.06 to 0.30 and peaked at 0.49 on 03-17 while black carbon and sulphate fell. Taken alone this looked like a usable surface dust indicator.
validation.full_record_check: Across the whole 2020-2025 record that impression does NOT hold. Dust AOD correlates with station PM10 at only r = +0.32 (dust_fraction: +0.20). The day with the highest dust AOD (2025-05-05, 1.86) had station PM10 of 50 ug/m3, while the record's strongest surface dust event (2021-03-15, station PM10 1765 ug/m3) ranks only 152nd of 2193 days by dust AOD. Decisively, the PM10/PM2.5 coarse-fraction ratio is identical between the 30 highest and 30 lowest dust-AOD days (2.60 vs 2.59): if the product were tracking surface dust, the coarse fraction would have to differ.
validation.interpretation: AOD is a column-integrated quantity and dust frequently travels in elevated layers that never reach the ground. The product is behaving correctly; using it as a surface indicator is the error.

intended_use: Column-integrated aerosol composition and its seasonality, including elevated transport layers that surface monitors cannot see.
Deliberate contrast material: the column-versus-surface mismatch documented above is a realistic analytical error, and this dataset paired with the station record makes it measurable.
known_limitations: Column AOD is NOT a surface concentration indicator. Dust AOD correlates with station PM10 at only r = +0.32 and misranks the record's strongest surface dust event to 152nd place. Never use dust_aod550 or dust_fraction to identify ground-level dust episodes.

dust_fraction measures composition, not amount. On clean days a small total AOD can be dust-dominated, so a high fraction does not imply a dust event: the highest-fraction days have station PM10 near the record median.

cams_pm2p5_ugm3 and cams_pm10_ugm3 are model surface fields on an 80 km grid and disagree with the station network by more than an order of magnitude during events (108 vs 1765 ug/m3 of PM10 on 2021-03-15). They must never be compared to station values as if measuring the same quantity, nor used to validate the observations.
Horizontal resolution is 0.75 degrees, so all twelve stations fall in the same one or two cells; no within-city analysis is possible.
Coverage ends 2025-12 because EAC4 has not released 2026, seven months short of the other Beijing datasets. Any statistic spanning 2026 silently loses this variable.
Temporal resolution is 3-hourly, not hourly, so it cannot be joined one-to-one with the hourly station record without an explicit resampling choice.
